title: Machine-learning models identify small-molecule opioid receptor activators and inhibitors
summary: Four machine-learning algorithms were trained on quantitative high-throughput screening data for three opioid receptors in agonist and antagonist modes; random forest performed best, with the mu-receptor agonist model reaching AUC-ROC 0.88 and MCC 0.7. Compounds predicted active by the best models were tested in the same qHTS assays, giving experimentally confirmed hit rates from 2.3% (delta agonist) to 15.8% (mu agonist), at least a 2-fold enrichment over the original assay hit rate. Potent hits were examined further by docking; confirmation used the same assay format that produced the training data.
ai_technology: Random forest and other machine-learning classifiers on chemical structures for virtual screening
organization: National Institutes of Health; George Mason University; National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences

evidence.tested: Model-predicted active compounds were tested in the same qHTS assays that generated the training data.
evidence.unknown: Selectivity, in vivo activity and effects beyond the screening assays; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models prioritized compounds from a large library for experimental testing.
